newsitem.title: INDIA: Banque Paribas neutral on Indian stocks.
newsitem.headline: Banque Paribas neutral on Indian stocks.

text.p: Banque Paribas said on Tuesday it changed its stance on Indian stocks to "neutral" from "buy" after Friday's market-friendly budget inspired boom.
The stocks rally was triggered by measures designed to boost the market rather than stronger fundamentals, a report by its international equity research arm said.
"We think the improvements overall are relatively small to have generated a 14 percent rise in the index in three days," it said. "We are getting nervous."
The Bombay Stock Exchange's top-30 index vaulted to a intraday peak of 4,007.91 on Monday before retreating sharply to 3,871.05 -- against 3,474.79 in pre-budget trade on Friday.
On Tuesday, the index ended 73.68 points, or 1.90 percent, higher at a provisional 3,944.73.
"We think this is a feeding frenzy and do not expect the market to hold at much over 4,000 at best," it said.

Allowing companies to buy back their own shares, removal of taxes on dividends in the hands of investors and higher foreign portfolio investment limits in Indian companies at 30 percent against 24 percent were the main factors that fuelled the rally, the report said.
Inflationary expectations will drive the market higher with investor demand for equity improving against debt.
"For foreign investors, inflationary expectations are a bit double-edged - it will put pressure on the rupee," it said.
"Overall, then we think this market is likely to top out soon, if not fall. We have a neutral stance at this time."
